basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Decimo enim mense prima die mensis apparuerunt cacumina montium. Potest dies prima decimi'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Decimo enim mense prima die mensis apparuerunt cacumina montium. Potest dies prima decimi mensis initium illud vitae perennis intelligi, quo etiam in hac vita positi gustant et vident sancti quoniam suavis est Dominus. In qua die apparent cacumina montium, quia quanto perfectius hoc in eorum mundo corde geritur, tanto certius mundana celsitudo quam frustra infletur patescit.
